subject: Decide whether rowt should warn or refuse on a reachable-but-too-slow lane
description:
Design question left deliberately open when BUG-corp-lane-throughput.md was resolved
(commit 163b15e, rowt 3.4.11). Not a defect — a policy decision that needs a ruling
before any code.

The report framed a lane that is REACHABLE but far too slow to use as a fail-closed
violation: rowt says the lane is up, the user's clone/pull crawls or dies, and nothing
in rowt's own output distinguishes "working" from "technically routed at 200 KB/s".
The 3.4.11 investigation exonerated rowt for that specific case — the same object
fetched with --noproxy '*' was no faster (226 KB/s through rowt vs 253 KB/s bypassed;
the direct lane runs ~32 MB/s), so the cause was the corp tunnel itself (utun11,
mtu 1294) — but the general question stands.

The question: should rowt warn, or refuse, when a lane is reachable but its throughput
is far below the other lanes? Sub-questions a decision has to answer:
  - warn only, or ever fail closed? (fail-closed on a slow lane can strand a user who
    genuinely has only that path)
  - what threshold, and relative to what — an absolute floor, or a ratio against the
    fastest lane measured in the same run?
  - where does it surface: `rowt status`, `rowt explain`, the monitor, or a watch-time
    notification?
  - does it belong to the reflex engine (a sensed input feeding profile selection)
    rather than to a one-shot command?

`rowt speed` (added 3.4.11) already produces the signal such a rule would consume:
per-lane VIA ROWT / BYPASSED throughput plus the predicted lane, using the same
_longest_domain_hit predictor as `explain`. So this is about policy, not measurement.

Read first: BUG-corp-lane-throughput.md (the Resolution section at the end),
FUTURE.md §5 "Sensing → deciding" and §10 "Open design questions" — this most likely
becomes a bullet there rather than a standalone feature.

Definition of done: a ruling recorded in FUTURE.md §10 (or DESIGN.md if it turns out
to belong to today's commands), with the threshold/surface decided or the idea
explicitly declined and why.
